transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (CISO, Crown), Marcus Hale (Cloud Architect), Samir Gupta (VP Eng)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery focused on whether Redwood Hosted can meet Crown's compliance (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA-ish controls), and what Dedicated/Private options look like for BYOK, HSM, VPC peering and audit log retention. Action items agreed at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. This is Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, and Ethan our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:07] Lena: Hi Maya, doing well. Thanks. We wanted to run through your security posture, especially how data is handled with hosted vs dedicated, and options for SSO/SAML and KMS.
[00:16] Maya: Totally, that's exactly why we're here. We usually start with high-level compliance certs then dig into encryption, auth, and logs. Ethan, want to kick off with certs?
[00:25] Ethan: Sure Redwood holds SOC 2 Type II and we have customers who've completed ISO 27001 assessments with our platform. We also maintain pen test reports and can share redacted summaries. For customers with strict requirements we offer Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments which give more control over networking and keys.
[00:40] Marcus: Quick question when you say "Dedicated" what is actually separated? Is it tenant isolation on shared infra or dedicated GPUs in a customer VPC?
[00:49] Ethan: Good question. For Redwood Dedicated, compute is isolated to your reserved pool you get dedicated GPU instances and dedicated runtime nodes. Networking still traverses our managed control plane unless you choose Private, where you can have a private control plane and VPC peering or on-prem. There are tradeoffs for maintenance/uptime and we can outline SLAs.
[01:10] Samir: And Private would be fully customer-managed networking and KMS? Would that be BYOK?
[01:15] Ethan: Yes, Private supports BYOK via integrations with customer KMS, and we also have HSM-backed options for enterprise customers. We can support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and bring-your-own-HSM flows for on-prem HSMs depending on deployment.
[01:28] Lena: Is the hosted API encrypting data at rest with your keys or mine? We need separation for certain datasets.
[01:34] Ethan: For Hosted, by default data at rest is encrypted with Redwood-managed keys. We offer Customer Key support on Dedicated tiers and Private where you can control keys. For strict separation and compliance we recommend Private with BYOK.
[01:45] Lena: OK. How about audit logs  we need immutable logs with a 7-year retention in some cases. What's typical?
[01:52] Maya: We store standard audit logs for API calls, model changes, and admin actions. Retention on hosted defaults to 90 days but for Dedicated and Private there are configurable retention policies and options to export logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or cloud storage for long-term retention.
[02:06] Marcus: Is export push or pull? Do you store copies after export?
[02:10] Ethan: We can push via streaming or exports. If you configure long-term retention we recommend exporting directly to your bucket we can disable retained copies on Redwood side in Private deployments. On Hosted we do keep minimal logs for operational debugging but we can redact or limit retention based on contract.
[02:26] Lena: We also need SSO  SAML with Okta is standard. Do you support SCIM for provisioning and role sync?
[02:32] Maya: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is available in the Console with roles like admin, billing, viewer, and custom roles for fine-grained permissions.
[02:42] Samir: On RBAC  can roles be scoped to projects/environments? We want developers to have different access than compliance auditors.
[02:48] Ethan: Absolutely  roles can be scoped per project and you can create role bindings for teams. For Private deployments you can map to your IdP groups via SCIM and have audit trails for role changes.
[02:59] Marcus: On encryption in flight  do you terminate TLS at your edge or can we enforce mTLS from our side?
[03:04] Ethan: TLS is enforced for all communications. For Private deployments with VPC peering we can enable mTLS and mutual CA validation for stricter network-level control.
[03:13] Lena: About SOC2 evidence  do you provide SOC2 Type II report and a list of controls mapped to your product features? We need that for our vendor attestation.
[03:21] Maya: We'll send the SOC2 Type II report and a controls matrix mapping to common frameworks. We'll also include a redacted pen test summary.
[03:29] Lena: Great. Also, incident response  what SLAs for incident notification and do you provide customer-facing postmortems?
[03:35] Ethan: We have incident notification policies  customers are notified within our contractual windows; for Dedicated and Private we can negotiate tighter SLA windows and incident call processes. Postmortems are shared at a level appropriate to the customer  we redact sensitive vendor details but include root cause and mitigations.
[03:52] Marcus: Network architecture  for Private do you support VPC endpoints and private links? We need no public internet exposure for inference traffic.
[03:59] Ethan: Yes, Private supports VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and Azure Private Link patterns. You can keep inference traffic inside your network. For Hosted we expose an API over TLS and can restrict access via IP allowlists and service tokens.
[04:12] Samir: Any compliance around data residency? Our research data needs to stay in EU.
[04:17] Maya: We have region controls and can provision Dedicated/Private in specific cloud regions. For Hosted we also offer EU-only processing regions; we can include that in the contract for data residency guarantees.
[04:29] Lena: One more  data retention and deletion. If we send PHI or sensitive patient-derived sequences, how quickly can you purge data, and do you provide proof of deletion?
[04:37] Ethan: For Private we can configure no data persistence on Redwood side and ensure logs and payloads are stored only in your systems. For Hosted, we have retention windows and deletion workflows  we can process deletion requests and provide attestations for data purge, but for strict PHI requirements customers typically choose Private or Dedicated with BYOK.
[04:58] Marcus: Are there any features that require telemetry to leave our environment? For example, model telemetry or fallback routing?
[05:04] Ethan: We do have optional telemetry for performance optimizations; it's opt-in and can be redacted. Fallback routing to cheaper model variants typically stays within the chosen region and doesn't require sending your data externally, but we can disable that for locked-down customers.
[05:19] Maya: Sounds like the decision points for you are: 1) whether Hosted meets your compliance once we provide SOC2 and retention SLAs, 2) whether Dedicated is enough for key control and isolation, or 3) Private for full BYOK and VPC/on-prem needs.
[05:33] Samir: Yes, timeline wise we want a procurement window by end of Q2 and a possible pilot in mid-Q2.
[05:40] Lena: We'll need pricing for Dedicated and Private and an architecture walkthrough to sign off with procurement.
[05:46] Maya: For next steps we'll send the SOC2 and ISO certs, a private deployment architecture diagram, and a draft pricing sheet for Dedicated/Private. We'll also schedule a technical deep-dive with your security team  what does two weeks look like for you?
[05:58] Marcus: Week of April 12th works.
[06:01] Maya: Great  Ethan, can you run through a quick list of docs we'll attach?
[06:06] Ethan: Sure  SOC2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate (if requested), pen test summary, architecture diagrams for Hosted/Dedicated/Private, KMS/HSM integration guide, and sample SLA language for retention and incident notification.
[06:22] Lena: Also send any references of customers in biotech regulated industries if you can.
[06:26] Maya: Will do.
[06:28] Samir: A couple of technical clarifications before we wrap  what about key rotation and auditability? If we manage keys, do you require a specific rotation cadence?
[06:36] Ethan: We support customer key rotation policies; if you use AWS KMS we can leverage automatic rotation or you can rotate and re-encrypt. We provide logs for key usage and can integrate with your KMS audit trails.
[06:48] Lena: For RBAC change logs  are those tamper-evident? We need an immutable trail for auditor reviews.
[06:54] Ethan: We provide append-only audit logs with integrity checks; in Private you can export to an immutable store in your environment for auditor access. For Hosted we sign logs and can provide attestations on request.
[07:08] Marcus: Perf question briefly  if we choose Dedicated with GPU pools, can you guarantee latency SLOs for model inference? We need 95th percentile under 300ms for short-context models.
[07:18] Maya: We publish performance profiles and for Dedicated can commit to tighter latency SLAs depending on reserved capacity. We'll include benchmark data in the doc pack.
[07:27] Samir: Good. That helps procurement.
[07:30] Lena: Anything else on compliance? HIPAA signatory for BAA  do you sign BAAs for Hosted?
[07:36] Maya: We do execute BAAs for Hosted and Dedicated for covered entities with the appropriate amendments. For Private on-prem it's customer-controlled but we support attestation language.
[07:47] Marcus: Ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[07:50] Maya: Recap: Maya will send SOC2, ISO cert, pen test summary, pricing sheet. Ethan will prepare architecture diagram and KMS/HSM integration notes. Crown to provide retention windows and list of required controls. Schedule deep-dive week of April 12th.
[08:06] Lena: Sounds good.
[08:08] Samir: Thanks, appreciate it.
[08:10] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with docs and calendar invite for the deep-dive.
[08:16] Marcus: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
